title: For better or for worse: the race where Finnish men carry their wives

words.note: 来自婚礼誓词 for better, for worse（无论顺境逆境）。日常也说“不管结果是好是坏”：For better or worse, the decision has been made.
words.ctx: For better or for worse: the race where Finnish men carry their wives

ex.en: [[For better or worse]], we're stuck with this car.
ex.zh: 不管好坏，我们只能用这辆车了。

ex.en: They promised to stay together [[for better or for worse]].
ex.zh: 他们承诺无论顺境逆境都要在一起。

words.def: whatever happens, whether the result is good or bad

cloze.before: For
cloze.after: or for worse: the race where Finnish men carry their wives
cloze.hint: 无论好坏（for ___ or for worse）
cloze.szh: 无论顺境还是逆境：芬兰男人背着妻子赛跑的比赛

words.note: 本义“困的”；形容城镇、村子时是“冷清、没什么活动”：a sleepy village（安静的小村庄）。
words.ctx: Every summer, a sleepy town in central Finland plays host to one of the world's oddest sporting events.

ex.en: We spent a week in a [[sleepy]] fishing village.
ex.zh: 我们在一个安静的渔村住了一周。

ex.en: The baby is getting [[sleepy]].
ex.zh: 宝宝开始犯困了。

words.def: (of a place) quiet, with not much activity; tired and ready to sleep

cloze.before: Every summer, a
cloze.after: town in central Finland plays host to one of the world's oddest sporting events.
cloze.szh: 每年夏天，芬兰中部一个安静的小镇都会举办一项全世界最古怪的体育赛事。

words.note: 作动词：stage an event / a concert / a protest（举办活动、音乐会、抗议）。名词是“舞台；阶段”。
words.ctx: Sonkajärvi, a town of a few thousand people, is not an obvious place to stage a world championship.

ex.en: The city will [[stage]] the next Olympic Games.
ex.zh: 这座城市将举办下一届奥运会。

ex.en: Workers [[staged]] a protest outside the factory.
ex.zh: 工人们在工厂外举行了抗议。

words.def: to organize an event, especially a public one; to perform a play

cloze.before: Sonkajärvi, a town of a few thousand people, is not an obvious place to
cloze.after: a world championship.
cloze.szh: 松卡耶尔维是个只有几千人的小镇，按理说不像是举办世界锦标赛的地方。

words.note: 很多人一下子来到某地：Fans descended on the stadium.（球迷涌向体育场。）也可以说亲戚“突然来访”。
words.ctx: Yet each July thousands of visitors descend on it to watch men sprint through mud with a woman slung over their shoulders.

ex.en: Thousands of tourists [[descend on]] the island every summer.
ex.zh: 每年夏天都有成千上万的游客涌上这座岛。

ex.en: My relatives [[descended on]] us for the holidays.
ex.zh: 假期亲戚们一窝蜂地来了我家。

words.def: (of a large number of people) to arrive at a place, often suddenly

cloze.before: Yet each July thousands of visitors
cloze.after: on it to watch men sprint through mud with a woman slung over their shoulders.
cloze.szh: 然而每年七月，成千上万的游客涌向这里，看男人们肩上扛着一个女人在泥地里飞奔。

words.note: 短距离全速跑：sprint for the bus（冲去赶公交）。名词 a sprint（短跑、冲刺）。
words.ctx: Yet each July thousands of visitors descend on it to watch men sprint through mud with a woman slung over their shoulders.

ex.en: I had to [[sprint]] to catch the last train.
ex.zh: 我得拼命跑才赶上末班车。

ex.en: She [[sprinted]] towards the finish line.
ex.zh: 她向终点线冲刺。

words.def: to run very fast for a short distance

cf.diff: jog 是为了锻炼慢慢地跑；sprint 是短距离用尽全力冲刺。

ex.en: I [[jog]] in the park every morning.
ex.zh: 我每天早上在公园慢跑。

cloze.before: Yet each July thousands of visitors descend on it to watch men
cloze.after: through mud with a woman slung over their shoulders.
cloze.szh: 然而每年七月，成千上万的游客涌向这里，看男人们肩上扛着一个女人在泥地里飞奔。

words.note: 过去式、过去分词都是 slung。sling a bag over your shoulder（把包往肩上一甩）。名词 sling 是“吊带、三角巾”。
words.ctx: Yet each July thousands of visitors descend on it to watch men sprint through mud with a woman slung over their shoulders.

ex.en: He [[slung]] his jacket over the back of the chair.
ex.zh: 他把外套往椅背上一搭。

ex.en: She walked in with a bag [[slung over]] her shoulder.
ex.zh: 她肩上挎着个包走了进来。

words.def: to put something somewhere in a careless or quick way, often over your shoulder

cloze.before: Yet each July thousands of visitors descend on it to watch men sprint through mud with a woman
cloze.after: over their shoulders.
cloze.hint: 挂在肩上（sling 的过去分词）
cloze.szh: 然而每年七月，成千上万的游客涌向这里，看男人们肩上扛着一个女人在泥地里飞奔。

words.note: 表示“起源”时常用复数：the origins of the festival。也指人的出身：of humble origins（出身卑微）。形容词 original。
words.ctx: Its origins, supposedly, lie in the 19th century.

ex.en: Nobody is sure about the [[origins]] of the song.
ex.zh: 没人确定这首歌的来历。

ex.en: The word has Latin [[origins]].
ex.zh: 这个词源自拉丁语。

words.def: the point or place where something begins; a person's family background

cloze.before: Its
cloze.after: , supposedly, lie in the 19th century.
cloze.szh: 据说它的起源可以追溯到 19 世纪。

words.note: 表示“大家都这么说”，但说话人带点怀疑：The house is supposedly haunted.（据说这房子闹鬼。）
words.ctx: Its origins, supposedly, lie in the 19th century.

ex.en: The film is [[supposedly]] based on a true story.
ex.zh: 据说这部电影是根据真实故事改编的。

ex.en: He's [[supposedly]] the best cook in town.
ex.zh: 据说他是镇上最好的厨师。

words.def: according to what is generally believed or said, although it may not be true

cf.diff: be supposed to do 常表示“应该做（按规定或计划）”：You're supposed to wear a helmet.；supposedly 是副词“据说”，不能表示“应该”。

ex.en: You're [[supposed to]] be at work by nine.
ex.zh: 你应该九点前到公司。

cloze.before: Its origins,
cloze.after: , lie in the 19th century.
cloze.szh: 据说它的起源可以追溯到 19 世纪。

words.note: 一个地方流传下来的故事、习俗和信仰，不可数：Irish folklore（爱尔兰民间传说）。
words.ctx: Local folklore tells of a robber called Herkko Rosvo-Ronkainen, who is said to have tested would-be members of his gang by making them carry heavy sacks through the forest.

ex.en: In local [[folklore]], the lake is home to a monster.
ex.zh: 根据当地传说，这湖里住着一只怪物。

ex.en: She studies Scandinavian [[folklore]].
ex.zh: 她研究斯堪的纳维亚的民间传说。

words.def: the traditional stories and beliefs of a community, passed on by word of mouth

cloze.before: Local
cloze.after: tells of a robber called Herkko Rosvo-Ronkainen, who is said to have tested would-be members of his gang by making them carry heavy sacks through the forest.
cloze.szh: 当地民间传说讲到一个叫赫尔科·罗斯沃-龙凯宁的强盗，据说他会让想入伙的人背着沉重的麻袋穿过森林，以此考验他们。

words.note: 放在名词前：would-be actors（想当演员的人）、a would-be thief（企图行窃的人）。
words.ctx: Local folklore tells of a robber called Herkko Rosvo-Ronkainen, who is said to have tested would-be members of his gang by making them carry heavy sacks through the forest.

ex.en: The course is popular with [[would-be]] writers.
ex.zh: 这门课很受想当作家的人欢迎。

ex.en: A [[would-be]] thief was caught by the shop owner.
ex.zh: 一个企图行窃的人被店主抓住了。

words.def: wanting or trying to be a particular type of person

cloze.before: Local folklore tells of a robber called Herkko Rosvo-Ronkainen, who is said to have tested
cloze.after: members of his gang by making them carry heavy sacks through the forest.
cloze.szh: 当地民间传说讲到一个叫赫尔科·罗斯沃-龙凯宁的强盗，据说他会让想入伙的人背着沉重的麻袋穿过森林，以此考验他们。

words.note: 多指虚构的、传说的或夸张的故事：fairy tale（童话）、tell tales（打小报告）。
words.ctx: Darker versions of the tale have his men raiding nearby villages and running off with women.

ex.en: Grandma told us [[tales]] of ghosts and witches.
ex.zh: 奶奶给我们讲鬼和女巫的故事。

ex.en: It's a [[tale]] of love and loss.
ex.zh: 这是一个关于爱与失去的故事。

words.def: a story, especially one that is imaginary or hard to believe

cf.diff: tale 和 tail 读音完全一样 /teɪl/：tale 是故事，tail 是尾巴。

ex.en: The dog wagged its [[tail]].
ex.zh: 狗摇了摇尾巴。

cloze.before: Darker versions of the
cloze.after: have his men raiding nearby villages and running off with women.
cloze.szh: 这个故事更阴暗的版本说，他的手下会袭击附近的村子，把女人抢走。

words.zh: 突袭、袭击；（警察）突击搜查
words.note: 动词、名词同形：a police raid（警察突击搜查）。口语还可以说 raid the fridge（翻冰箱找吃的）。
words.ctx: Darker versions of the tale have his men raiding nearby villages and running off with women.

ex.en: Police [[raided]] the building at dawn.
ex.zh: 警察在黎明时突袭了这栋楼。

ex.en: The kids [[raided]] the fridge after school.
ex.zh: 孩子们放学后把冰箱翻了个遍。

words.def: to attack a place suddenly; (of police) to enter a place suddenly to search it

cf.diff: invade 是军队大规模“入侵、占领”一个国家；raid 是短时间的“突袭”，打完就走。

ex.en: The army [[invaded]] the country.
ex.zh: 军队入侵了这个国家。

cloze.before: Darker versions of the tale have his men
cloze.after: nearby villages and running off with women.
cloze.szh: 这个故事更阴暗的版本说，他的手下会袭击附近的村子，把女人抢走。

words.zh: （故事、说法里）描写某人在做……；让某人一直做……
words.note: have + 宾语 + doing：①（某个版本、故事）把某人写成在做……：The legend has him living in a cave.（传说中他住在山洞里。）②让某人持续做某事：He had us laughing all night.（他让我们笑了一整晚。）
words.ctx: Darker versions of the tale have his men raiding nearby villages and running off with women.

ex.en: The old story [[has]] the king hiding in a tree.
ex.zh: 那个古老的故事里，国王躲在一棵树上。

ex.en: The comedian [[had]] us laughing all night.
ex.zh: 那位喜剧演员让我们笑了一整晚。

words.conn: 主语（故事、版本、人）+ have + 宾语 + doing

pick.q: The film ___ the hero living alone on an island.
pick.why: “电影把主角描写成独自住在岛上”，用 have sb doing。make sb do 后接动词原形。

pick.q: Within minutes, the clown had the children ___.
pick.why: have sb doing：让某人一直在做……，用 -ing。

cloze.before: Darker versions of the tale
cloze.after: his men raiding nearby villages and running off with women.
cloze.hint: 描写某人在做……（___ his men raiding）
cloze.szh: 这个故事更阴暗的版本说，他的手下会袭击附近的村子，把女人抢走。

words.note: be anyone's guess：没人知道答案：What happens next is anyone's guess.（接下来会怎样谁也说不准。）
words.ctx: Whether any of this happened is anyone's guess; the town is happy to cash in on the legend either way.

ex.en: Why he left is [[anyone's guess]].
ex.zh: 他为什么走，谁也说不准。

ex.en: When the train will arrive is [[anyone's guess]].
ex.zh: 火车什么时候到，谁也不知道。

words.def: something that nobody can know for certain

cloze.before: Whether any of this happened is anyone's
cloze.after: ; the town is happy to cash in on the legend either way.
cloze.szh: 这些事有没有发生过，谁也说不准；不管怎样，小镇都乐于借这个传说赚钱。

words.note: 趁机利用某个机会赚钱，常带点贬义：Shops cash in on the World Cup.（商店借世界杯赚钱。）
words.ctx: Whether any of this happened is anyone's guess; the town is happy to cash in on the legend either way.

ex.en: Hotels [[cash in on]] the festival by raising prices.
ex.zh: 酒店借节日涨价赚钱。

ex.en: He was accused of [[cashing in on]] his famous name.
ex.zh: 他被指责利用自己的名气捞好处。

words.def: to make money or gain an advantage from a situation, often unfairly

cloze.before: Whether any of this happened is anyone's guess; the town is happy to
cloze.after: in on the legend either way.
cloze.szh: 这些事有没有发生过，谁也说不准；不管怎样，小镇都乐于借这个传说赚钱。

words.note: scoff at sth：嘲笑、不屑：People scoffed at the idea.（人们对这个主意嗤之以鼻。）英式口语里还可指“狼吞虎咽”。
words.ctx: Historians may scoff, but a good story has never hurt tourism.

ex.en: They [[scoffed]] at my plan, but it worked.
ex.zh: 他们嘲笑我的计划，可它成功了。

ex.en: Don't [[scoff]]; it could happen.
ex.zh: 别不屑，这是有可能的。

words.def: to laugh at or talk about something in a way that shows you think it is stupid

cf.diff: 形近词：scoff 是“嘲笑、不屑”；scold 是“责骂（孩子等）”。

ex.en: His mum [[scolded]] him for being late.
ex.zh: 他妈妈骂他回来晚了。

cloze.before: Historians may
cloze.after: , but a good story has never hurt tourism.
cloze.szh: 历史学家也许会嗤之以鼻，但一个好故事从来不会对旅游业有坏处。

words.zh: 以……为特色、包含；（电影等）由……主演
words.note: 作动词：The hotel features a rooftop pool.（酒店的特色是有个屋顶泳池。）名词是“特点、特征”。
words.ctx: The course is 253.5 metres long and features two dry obstacles and a water pit about a metre deep.

ex.en: The new phone [[features]] a larger screen.
ex.zh: 新手机配备了更大的屏幕。

ex.en: The film [[features]] several famous actors.
ex.zh: 这部电影有好几位明星出演。

words.def: to include something as an important part

cloze.before: The course is 253.5 metres long and
cloze.after: two dry obstacles and a water pit about a metre deep.
cloze.szh: 赛道长 253.5 米，有两个陆地障碍和一个大约一米深的水坑。

words.note: 可以是真实的障碍物（obstacle course 障碍赛道），也可以是抽象的困难：an obstacle to success（成功路上的障碍）。
words.ctx: The course is 253.5 metres long and features two dry obstacles and a water pit about a metre deep.

ex.en: Money is the biggest [[obstacle]] to our plans.
ex.zh: 钱是我们计划最大的障碍。

ex.en: The horse jumped over every [[obstacle]].
ex.zh: 那匹马跳过了每一个障碍。

words.def: something that blocks your way or makes it difficult to do something

cloze.before: The course is 253.5 metres long and features two dry
cloze.after: and a water pit about a metre deep.
cloze.szh: 赛道长 253.5 米，有两个陆地障碍和一个大约一米深的水坑。

words.note: or, indeed, ...：用来补充一个更进一步的说法，“甚至……”。也可加强语气：Thank you very much indeed.（真的非常感谢。）
words.ctx: The "wife" does not have to be married to the carrier, or, indeed, to anyone.

ex.en: Few people, [[indeed]] almost nobody, came.
ex.zh: 来的人很少，其实几乎没人来。

ex.en: It was a very good meal [[indeed]].
ex.zh: 这顿饭真的很好吃。

words.def: used to add a stronger point; used to emphasize that something is true

cloze.before: The "wife" does not have to be married to the carrier, or,
cloze.after: , to anyone.
cloze.szh: 这位“妻子”不一定要和背她的人结婚，事实上，她跟谁结没结婚都无所谓。

words.note: be weighed down with/by：被……压着（字面或比喻）：weighed down with shopping（提着一大堆购物袋）、weighed down by worries（忧心忡忡）。
words.ctx: She must, however, be over 17 and weigh at least 49kg; anyone lighter is weighed down with a rucksack of ballast to make up the difference.

ex.en: She was [[weighed down]] with heavy bags.
ex.zh: 她拎着沉重的袋子。

ex.en: He felt [[weighed down]] by his debts.
ex.zh: 他被债务压得喘不过气。

words.def: to make someone or something heavy; to make someone feel worried

cloze.after: down with a rucksack of ballast to make up the difference.
cloze.szh: 不过，她必须年满 17 岁，体重至少 49 公斤；不够重的人要背一个装着配重的背包，把差的重量补上。

words.note: 船、热气球等为了平稳而装的重物；这里指为了达到体重要求而背的重物。不可数。
words.ctx: She must, however, be over 17 and weigh at least 49kg; anyone lighter is weighed down with a rucksack of ballast to make up the difference.

ex.en: The ship carried rocks as [[ballast]].
ex.zh: 这艘船装着石头当压舱物。

ex.en: The balloon rose when they dropped the [[ballast]].
ex.zh: 他们扔掉配重后，气球升了起来。

words.def: heavy material carried to make something more stable or to add weight

cloze.before: She must, however, be over 17 and weigh at least 49kg; anyone lighter is weighed down with a rucksack of
cloze.after: to make up the difference.
cloze.szh: 不过，她必须年满 17 岁，体重至少 49 公斤；不够重的人要背一个装着配重的背包，把差的重量补上。

words.note: 比 choose 正式：opt for sth / opt to do sth。opt out（选择不参加）。名词 option（选项）。
words.ctx: Most teams opt for the so-called Estonian carry, in which the wife hangs upside down with her legs around the man's neck and her arms clasped around his waist.

ex.en: Most people [[opt for]] the cheaper ticket.
ex.zh: 大多数人会选便宜的票。

ex.en: We [[opted for]] a quiet wedding.
ex.zh: 我们选择了一场简单的婚礼。

words.def: to choose one thing instead of others

cf.diff: choose 最普通；opt for 稍正式，强调“在几个选项中经过考虑选了某一个”。

ex.en: [[Choose]] a card, any card.
ex.zh: 选一张牌，随便哪张。

cloze.before: Most teams
cloze.after: for the so-called Estonian carry, in which the wife hangs upside down with her legs around the man's neck and her arms clasped around his waist.
cloze.szh: 大多数队伍选择所谓的“爱沙尼亚背法”：妻子头朝下倒挂，双腿勾住男人的脖子，双臂紧紧抱住他的腰。

words.note: 上下颠倒：hang upside down（倒挂）。比喻“弄得乱七八糟”：turn the house upside down（把家翻得乱七八糟）。
words.ctx: Most teams opt for the so-called Estonian carry, in which the wife hangs upside down with her legs around the man's neck and her arms clasped around his waist.

ex.en: The picture is hanging [[upside down]].
ex.zh: 这幅画挂倒了。

ex.en: We turned the house [[upside down]] looking for the keys.
ex.zh: 我们为了找钥匙把家里翻了个底朝天。

words.def: with the top part at the bottom; in a very untidy state

cf.diff: upside down 是上下颠倒；inside out 是里外翻过来（衣服穿反了）。

ex.en: You're wearing your jumper [[inside out]].
ex.zh: 你的毛衣穿反了。

cloze.before: Most teams opt for the so-called Estonian carry, in which the wife hangs
cloze.after: down with her legs around the man's neck and her arms clasped around his waist.
cloze.szh: 大多数队伍选择所谓的“爱沙尼亚背法”：妻子头朝下倒挂，双腿勾住男人的脖子，双臂紧紧抱住他的腰。

words.note: 用手或手臂紧紧握住、抱住：clasp your hands（双手紧握）。名词是“搭扣、扣子”。
words.ctx: Most teams opt for the so-called Estonian carry, in which the wife hangs upside down with her legs around the man's neck and her arms clasped around his waist.

ex.en: She [[clasped]] the letter to her chest.
ex.zh: 她把信紧紧贴在胸前。

ex.en: He sat with his hands [[clasped]] in his lap.
ex.zh: 他双手交握放在腿上坐着。

words.def: to hold something or someone tightly with your hands or arms

cf.diff: grasp 是“一把抓住”，还可以表示“理解”；clasp 强调“紧紧抱住、握住不放”，常带情感。

ex.en: She [[grasped]] the rope with both hands.
ex.zh: 她双手抓住了绳子。

cloze.before: Most teams opt for the so-called Estonian carry, in which the wife hangs upside down with her legs around the man's neck and her arms
cloze.after: around his waist.
cloze.szh: 大多数队伍选择所谓的“爱沙尼亚背法”：妻子头朝下倒挂，双腿勾住男人的脖子，双臂紧紧抱住他的腰。

words.note: dignified（庄重的、有尊严的）加 un-。常用来形容姿势、行为难看、丢脸。
words.ctx: It looks undignified, but it frees up the carrier's hands and keeps the weight close to his back.

ex.en: Falling off the stage was rather [[undignified]].
